$comment: Every performance budget in the project, in one place.
PLAN.md §10.6 states six budgets in prose. This file is the executable form: one entry per
metric, each with the id a test must emit for the number to be collected. Scripts/bench.sh
runs the benchmark lane, collects every '@@OPENSHEETS_BENCH@@' line, joins it against this
file, and writes docs/perf/latest.json. A metric declared here that nobody emitted appears in
the output as 'blocked' rather than quietly vanishing — a budget nobody is measuring is worse
than a budget nobody wrote down, because it looks like it is being watched.
TO ADD A MEASUREMENT: from any test target,
Benchmark.record(id: "grid.scroll.frame.p99.seconds", value: seconds, unit: .seconds)
and it lands in the report. `blockedOn` here is documentation, not a switch: emit the id and
the metric becomes 'measured' on the next run with no change to this file.
IDS ARE A CONTRACT. The baseline is keyed on them, so renaming one silently drops the metric
from the comparison instead of failing. Add a new id and retire the old one instead.
'unit' must be one of: seconds, milliseconds, bytes, count, ratio, rate.
'budget' is the ceiling (or floor, for ratio and rate); null means 'tracked, not gated'.
'noisy': true moves a metric from the strict tolerance to the timing one. Reserve it for a
measurement that is genuinely jittery - an RSS delta, say - never for one that is merely
inconvenient.
TWO TOLERANCES, BOTH MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED. Five back-to-back runs of this suite on
the Wave 1 development machine, at 2.5-3x its core count in load: counts and byte sizes
moved 0.0-0.3%, wall-clock metrics moved 3-29%. So counts are gated at 10% and timings at
20%, and on a machine whose load exceeds its core count the timing gate widens further and
says so out loud. Express a budget as a count wherever the question allows it.

metrics.blockedOn: SheetFormat's xlsx reader and GridKit's first layout pass
metrics.description: Wall clock from open() to the first frame that shows cells. Not the full parse: first paint is what the user experiences.
Full parse of Fixtures/perf/1m-cells.xlsx into a Workbook.
Peak resident size across the parse. Use WorkCounters.peakResidentBytes(): a reader that briefly holds two copies is over budget even if it frees one.
99th percentile frame time while flinging. 8.3 ms is one 120 Hz frame.
A count, not a duration — it stays honest on a loaded machine, which a frame-time percentile does not.
From the key event to the repainted cell.
One edit at the root of a 10,000-cell dependency graph, to a settled sheet.
Cells the recalculation visited. The load-proof twin of the metric above: a recalc that visits the whole sheet instead of the dependency closure shows up here even on a busy machine.
From the filesystem event to a WorkbookDiff ready to render.
Building a 1000 × 1000 CellStore. The floor under the reader's own budget: whatever A1 spends parsing is on top of this.
Resident bytes for a million cells in the model alone.
Measured residency divided by cell count. Near 128 means the container costs more than the contents.

metrics.planReference: §10.6 — component of the scroll frame budget
metrics.description: One screen of cells read out of a million. The grid does this every frame.

metrics.planReference: work-done form of the scroll budget
metrics.description: Heap blocks retained by the allocation-free walk over one screen. Must not scale with the 2,500 cells.
100k cells scattered across the whole 1,048,576 × 16,384 grid. Cost must track population, not bounding box.
Reading every cell of that sparse sheet through cells(in: .entireSheet).

metrics.planReference: §10.6 — model-level floor under 'external change → diff shown'
metrics.description: CellChange.classify over a 100k-cell rectangle with 500 changes in it.
How many addresses the diff looked at. A diff bound by the rectangle rather than by the populated rows shows up here.
How many cells the perturbation moved. A determinism canary: this number changing means the generator did, and every other number in the run is suspect.
A million CellRef(a1:) parses — one per cell on a 1M-cell open.
A million appendA1(to:) emissions — one per cell on a 1M-cell save.

metrics.planReference: §10.6 — component of the scroll frame budget
metrics.description: 10,000 offset↔index round-trips at row 1,048,575. Roughly ten seconds of flinging.
The run count the metric above is bound by. If this grows, that one grows with it and the cause is here.
10,000 CellStyle interns against a table of 400 distinct styles.

A fixed CPU kernel, timed. Not a budget — the divisor. Scripts/bench.sh normalises every seconds-valued metric by this run's value over the baseline's, which is what lets a number taken on a laptop be compared with one taken on a CI runner.
One-minute load average per core when the run was taken. Recorded so a surprising number can be explained rather than argued about.
Active processor count.
